Notes chapters for a course

Source: R/toolkit-chapter.R
copy_chapter.Rd

copy_chapter() copies a chapter of the mirtverse online book into the course's chapters/ folder so you can edit it. new_chapter() starts a blank chapter with the same headings as the book's chapters ("Learning goals", "Key terms", "Example 1", "Example 2", "Your turn", "In the lab", "Further reading"). swap_chapter_data() replaces the code that loads an example's data.

Usage

copy_chapter(id, course = ".", from = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

new_chapter(
  id,
  course = ".",
  title = NULL,
  data_code = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

swap_chapter_data(chapter, chunk = NULL, code)

book_chapters()

Arguments

id

the chapter's id. For copy_chapter(), one of book_chapters()$id; for new_chapter(), a new id (letters, digits, - and _).

course

the course folder.

from

where to copy from: A local copy of the book's source folder (book/ in the package's GitHub repository), or NULL (the default) to download the chapter from GitHub.

overwrite

replace an existing file. copy_chapter() also copies the book's _common.R (packages, chunk options and seed, sourced before each chapter) into chapters/ the first time, and check_material() runs it before a chapter's chunks.

title

the chapter title.

data_code

R code that loads the examples' data. It should define resp, a data frame of scored item responses. Defaults to the LSAT7 data from mirt.

chapter

the chapter's .Rmd file.

chunk

the label of the data chunk to replace, for example "data-dif-1". NULL (the default) replaces every data- chunk.

code

the new R code for the chunk(s).

Value

copy_chapter() and new_chapter() return the chapter's path, invisibly. book_chapters() returns a tibble with the id, file and title of each book chapter.

Details

Each example in a book chapter opens with a chunk labelled data-<chapter>-<n> that loads its data, and the rest of the example uses what that chunk defines. To use your own data, rewrite that chunk; the easiest way is swap_chapter_data().

See also

new_course(), check_material()

Examples

book_chapters()
#> # A tibble: 20 × 3
#>    id             file                  title                                   
#>    <chr>          <chr>                 <chr>                                   
#>  1 measurement    01-measurement.Rmd    Measurement, scoring and classical item…
#>  2 irt-models     02-irt-models.Rmd     From classical test theory to IRT       
#>  3 estimation     03-estimation.Rmd     Estimation and comparing models         
#>  4 dimensionality 04-dimensionality.Rmd Dimensionality and local independence   
#>  5 fit            05-fit.Rmd            Item fit, person fit and item quality   
#>  6 information    06-information.Rmd    Information, precision and reliability  
#>  7 scoring        07-scoring.Rmd        Scoring people                          
#>  8 polytomous     08-polytomous.Rmd     Polytomous items and open-ended respons…
#>  9 dif            09-dif.Rmd            Differential item functioning and fairn…
#> 10 linking        10-linking.Rmd        Linking and equating                    
#> 11 banks-cat      11-banks-cat.Rmd      Item banks, test assembly and adaptive …
#> 12 reporting      12-reporting.Rmd      Cut scores, reporting and communicating…
#> 13 ml-lens        13-ml-lens.Rmd        Machine learning through an IRT lens    
#> 14 item-text      14-item-text.Rmd      What item text tells us                 
#> 15 aig            15-aig.Rmd            Generating items                        
#> 16 auto-scoring   16-auto-scoring.Rmd   Automated scoring                       
#> 17 llms           17-llms.Rmd           Large language models as a colleague    
#> 18 ai-validity    18-ai-validity.Rmd    Validity, fairness and governance of AI 
#> 19 datasets       90-datasets.Rmd       Appendix: the datasets                  
#> 20 adapting       91-adapting.Rmd       Appendix: adapting the book             
course <- file.path(tempdir(), "chapter-demo")
ch <- new_chapter("my-week", course, title = "Our own data",
                  data_code = "resp <- expand.table(LSAT7)")
swap_chapter_data(ch, code = "resp <- expand.table(LSAT6)")
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
copy_chapter("dif", course)   # downloads from GitHub
} # }
